Subject: Post-demo follow-up: target unit pricing & vendor benchmarking (Acme Health)

Hi Jordan — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the pricing items we discussed so we can align next steps.

Summary of what you shared (please correct anything I missed):
- Monthly estimated traffic: ~60M tokens total (15M prompt, 45M completion) — peaks up to ~120M in a month.
- Critical SLOs: p95 latency < 250ms for single-turn inference, multi-turn chat acceptable at p95 < 400ms.
- Budget/target range: you indicated a desire to get to a sustainable unit cost that supports product pricing; you flagged $/1M token target in the low-mid double digits (ballpark).
- Security/compliance: must run in a private VPC for PHI-adjacent workflows (we covered Private deployment options).

Vendor/unit benchmarking (high-level):
- OpenAI (managed): representative commercial rates other customers see ~ $28–$40 per 1M tokens for the class of model you demoed (high-quality chat).
- Anthropic (managed): typically in the same band, often a touch below OpenAI for some usages (~ $25–$35 /1M).
- Open-model hosts / self-hosted quantized variants: wide range; low-cost hosts can be in the $10–$20 /1M ballpark but often trade off either latency, throughput, or support (and may need reserved infra to be stable).

Our recommended starting targets for Acme given your volumes and SLOs:
- On-demand (no commit): $30 / 1M tokens (fastest route, minimal commitment).
- Committed 12-month reserved plan (monthly committed tokens): $18 / 1M tokens — assumes a 40%+ monthly utilization of the committed pool and ability to route lower-priority traffic to lower-cost variants.
- Aggressive reserved (12–24 month, higher commit): $12–$15 / 1M tokens — requires higher commit and a short technical PoC to validate prefix/KV reuse to realize these unit costs.

Rationale (short):
- Redwood’s runtime reductions (KV/prefix caching + continuous batching) typically lower effective unit cost vs naive self-hosting, and the committed pricing levers let us offer material discounts vs managed providers while preserving the latency profile you need.

Action items / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the monthly committed token band you’d be comfortable evaluating for a pilot? (Options: 200M, 500M, 1B/month).
2) We’ll send a formal pricing estimate + an attached token-model workbook that shows net $/1M under different utilization and latency weightings.
3) If committed pricing looks good, propose a 30-day PoC with a 3-week ramp to validate p95 latency and RU cost.

Attachments: ACME_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf (pricing breakdown), acme_token_model_v1.xlsx (volume sensitivity).

Thanks — looping in Marissa on procurement and Dylan on infra sizing.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
